findings.title: Customer asks for guidance on maximizing product usage
findings.description: Ben asks whether there is more he should be doing to get value from BetterBark, estimating he's only using about 40% of what the platform offers. This is a general request for usage/coaching guidance rather than a specific product defect or missing capability. Derek responds with two suggestions (goal-tracking feature, informal peer group) rather than any product change.
findings.quote: is there anything I should be doing to get more out of it? I feel like I'm probably using like 40% of what this thing can do.
findings.severity_reason: No defect or feature gap is described; purely a request for usage guidance.
findings.match_note: Not a defect/feature request; distinct from all catalogue items.

findings.title: Customer considers enabling existing goal-tracking feature after being told about it
findings.description: Derek tells Ben about the existing goal-tracking feature (members set a training goal with their coach and track it over a quarter). Ben says he knew it existed but hadn't promoted it, and after hearing the description decides his checklist-oriented staff might respond well to it and agrees to try it. No defect or missing capability is raised; this is adoption of an already-available feature that was introduced by the internal rep, not requested by the customer.
findings.quote: I know it exists. I haven't pushed it. Is it worth it?
findings.match_note: Feature already exists and is not in the tracked catalogue as a gap; no action needed.

findings.title: Positive feedback on scheduling ease-of-use; no change requested
findings.description: Ben volunteers that the mobile scheduling flow is easy enough for his least tech-savvy store manager to independently book sessions, explicitly framing the remark as 'not a complaint, it's a compliment.' He separately recounts that this same manager (Gary) prints and laminates the coaching schedule for the break-room wall despite it being fully available in the app, describing it fondly as Gary's own workflow rather than a product shortcoming. No product change is requested.
findings.quote: the scheduling is easy enough that even my least-techy manager, a guy who still prints his emails, books his own sessions.
findings.severity_reason: Explicitly framed by the customer as a compliment/observation, not a request for change.
findings.match_note: Positive, non-actionable feedback; not matched to any catalogue defect.

findings.title: Possible future seat expansion for a tenth store
findings.description: Ben mentions that a tenth store is a possible (unsigned) plan for next year, which would require a few additional license seats if it happens. This is a commercial/seat-count matter rather than a product defect or feature request; Ben says he will flag the account team once it's confirmed.
findings.quote: Store ten is a maybe for next year, nothing signed. If it happens I'll need a few more seats but we're not there.
findings.severity_reason: Commercial/account matter, not a product issue.
findings.match_note: Not a product defect or feature request; no catalogue match applicable.
